title: Poe-Llamanzares v. COMELEC
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that foundlings are considered natural-born citizens of the Philippines, allowing Senator Grace Poe to run for president. The Court held that international law and the Constitution support the presumption that foundlings born in the Philippines are natural-born Filipino citizens.
doctrine: Foundlings are, as a class, natural-born citizens. There is no legal or constitutional basis to discriminate against foundlings as the Constitution does not deny foundlings the status of natural-born citizenship. International conventions and customary law support the presumption that foundlings found in a state are citizens of that state.
citedStatutes: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
1961 Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness
fullText:
PEREZ, J.:

The issue is whether petitioner Mary Grace Natividad S. Poe-Llamanzares, a foundling, is a natural-born citizen of the Philippines and therefore qualified to run for president.

Section 1, Article IV of the 1987 Constitution provides that citizens of the Philippines are those who are citizens at the time of the adoption of the Constitution, those whose fathers or mothers are citizens, those born before January 17, 1973, of Filipino mothers, and those who are naturalized.

The Court holds that foundlings are natural-born citizens. To hold otherwise would create a class of stateless persons and violate international conventions to which the Philippines is a signatory.
